title: Backtracking
summary: Searching through every possibility, cleverly - the choose, explore, unchoose pattern, generating subsets, permutations and combinations, the N-queens puzzle with constant-time safety checks, solving Sudoku, pruning dead ends early, branch and bound, and a first look at NP-complete problems, where exhaustive search is the best known exact method.

cards.q: What are the three steps inside a backtracking loop?
cards.a:
choose, explore, unchoose

Apply a choice, recurse, then undo it so the next choice starts from the same state.

cards.q: How does the N-queens solver check diagonals in O(1)?
cards.a:
With arrays indexed by row + col and row - col

Squares on one diagonal share row + col, and on the other row - col, so one boolean array per direction records whether a queen is there.

cards.q: What does branch and bound add to backtracking?
cards.a:
Pruning branches that cannot beat the best

It abandons partial solutions whose best possible outcome cannot beat the best solution found so far, which prunes large parts of the search tree.
